post.title: Educational opportunities for Afghan students
post.description: Guidance to know study options, scholarships and prepare a clear path to continue studying abroad.
post.imageAlt: Students in a modern educational environment

postDetail.highlight: For an Afghan applicant, the study path starts from the evaluation of the goal, budget, grades and language and continues until the choice of destination, admission, visa and the beginning of student life. Double-check any terms and conditions at the destination's official source.

sections.title: 1. Assess your circumstances and goals
sections.body: Before searching for a university, specify the course, field, start date and the result you want to achieve. Don't think of the budget as just tuition; Also consider the cost of application, translation, language test, travel, insurance, accommodation and living. If budget is tight, list low-cost programs and scholarship options first.
items: Specify section, field and desired start date
Write the first year budget and emergency reserve separately
Clarify the career goal and the reason for choosing the field
For each option, record the formal condition and deadline

sections.title: 2. Compare the country, field and university
sections.body: Create three to six real applications and compare the language of instruction, GPA requirement, course prerequisites, degree credit, tuition, city fees, student work opportunities, and visa path separately. Read the official page of the university and the program itself; Rank or promotion alone is not enough reason to choose.
items: Save the official link, deadline and cost of each program
Match the prerequisites with your academic background
Compare the actual cost of the first year with the affordability
Have one main choice and two backup options

sections.title: 3. Plan the necessary language and exams
sections.body: Find out if the university accepts IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or other tests and what the minimum overall score and score for each skill is. Some programs also require an internal test, interview, GRE, GMAT, or portfolio. Coordinate the time of the test and receiving the result with the admission deadline.
items: Check the language requirements of the same program
Allow time to prepare and repeat the test
Write the minimum total score and each skill separately
Keep the official result and its validity date

sections.title: 4. Prepare standard and traceable documents
sections.body: The usual list includes passport, identity document, diploma, report card, graduation certificate, official translation, resume, motivation letter and recommendation letter; The final list is determined by the university. The name, date of birth and the order of education must be the same in all documents. Keep originals, translations, scans and shipping receipts organized.
items: Make a separate checklist for each university
Start translation and verification before the deadline
Personalize the motivation letter for the same major
Do not submit incomplete documents or incorrect information

sections.title: 5. Track admission and scholarship separately
sections.body: Submit the admission application from the official portal and keep your application number, payment receipt and email. University acceptance is not automatically a scholarship. For each scholarship, read tuition coverage, stipend, insurance, accommodation, payment period and deadline; Some scholarships are applied for at the same time as admission and some after.
items: Review the form and files before the deadline
Read the conditions of conditional admission carefully
Calculate the amount and costs not covered
Don't pay for a promise of acceptance or scholarship through an anonymous broker

sections.title: 6. Plan your visa and start your student life
sections.body: Once accepted, check the program name, start date, tuition, remaining requirements, and approval deadline. Then get the list of visa, financial ability, insurance, translation and residence only from the official website of the embassy or immigration office. University acceptance does not guarantee visa issuance and no false documents or false information is acceptable.
items: Record the deadline for confirmation of acceptance and payment of the deposit
Prepare financial documents and source of money according to regulations
Keep the original documents and their digital copies
Read the embassy's official conditions again before proceeding

sections.title: 7. Be prepared before traveling and after arrival
sections.body: Check accommodation, insurance, tickets, reception, university registration, bank account and transportation before you travel. After entering, do residence registration, final registration, unit selection and introduction meeting according to the university's instructions. For the first month, keep an emergency budget and the necessary numbers of the destination ready.
items: Match the address of the university and the place of residence with the travel time
Keep backups of documents and insurance online
Read the student work conditions from the official source
Record university deadlines in the calendar

post.title: Migration routes; From choosing the way to staying
post.description: A practical guide to comparing educational, work and family immigration, preparing your case and distinguishing valid information from false promises.
post.imageAlt: A view of an immigrant-friendly city

postDetail.highlight: Immigration is a legal and financial decision, not an immediate promise. First, determine the purpose and the legal route, then compare the official conditions of the destination country, cost, time, documents and the risk of rejection with your case.

sections.title: 1. Determine your goal and legal path
sections.body: Education, work, joining the family and investment are not the same conditions. Enter your purpose, age, education, work experience, language, budget and family status and check only the routes that exist in the law of the destination country.
items: Specify the type of accommodation and the expected result
Make the official page of the immigration office of the destination the main source
Do not apply for illegal routes or log in with false information
Check the possible cost and time before paying

sections.title: 2. Adjust conditions, points and documents
sections.body: In each program, the language requirement, education, work experience, job offer, financial ability, medical examination and bad history may be different. Create a table of documents and verify each item from an official source or authorized representative.
items: Check the official translation and validity of the documents
Check the validity date of your passport and certificates
Keep original and digital copies of documents
Get a written receipt from the consultant about the contract, cost and service scope

sections.title: 3. Understand the application, visa and residence separately
sections.body: Registering a profile, receiving an invitation or acceptance, applying for residence and issuing a visa are different steps. Receiving a letter of acceptance or a job offer does not guarantee a visa. Fill out forms completely and honestly, keep receipts and use only official time and payment channels.
items: Record the case number and response deadline
Check the email and portal to request additional documents
Avoid guaranteeing acceptance or visa with immediate payment
Read the negative decision and the way to protest from the official letter

sections.title: 4. After logging in, save your status
sections.body: After arrival, take address registration, insurance, extension of stay, working conditions, taxes and family obligations seriously. Read the law of work, education or change of employer from an official source; Ignoring the extension deadline can jeopardize the residence status.
items: Record the renewal deadline and terms of stay in the calendar
Archive official documents and correspondence
Refrain from working or studying outside the residence permit
Check again for updated information from the destination government

postDetail.sourcesNote: Immigration conditions change based on the country, type of residence and date of application; The official source of the destination government is the final reference.

post.title: Work abroad; From resume preparation to work permit
post.description: A practical guide to find legal work, evaluate a job offer, prepare documents and understand the responsibilities of a migrant worker.

postDetail.highlight: A job offer alone is not a work or residence permit. Check destination country, job, employer, contract, language, skills and license type before paying or leaving your country.

sections.title: 1. Choose the right job and country
sections.body: Specify your job title, technical skills, background, language and professional qualifications. Market demand and professional licensing requirements for doctors, nurses, engineers and regulated professions are different from general professions.
items: Match the resume to the actual job description
Check the professional degree and the possibility of equivalence
Extract the job language level from the official advertisement or law
Compare salary after tax and cost of living

sections.title: 2. Verify the job offer
sections.body: Check the employer's legal name, address, contract, gross and net salary, hours, location, insurance, vacation, probationary period and hiring costs. A real employer usually has a formal process and a clear contract for legal employment; Paying money to "guarantee a job" is a serious warning.
items: Ask for a written and translatable contract
Separate costs paid by the employer or the applicant
Do not leave the passport to an intermediary
Match the ad and email with the employer's official domain

sections.title: 3. Get work permit and visa from official source
sections.body: License conditions may be dependent on a job offer, skill shortage list, minimum salary, language test, quota or employer approval. Job offer, entry permit, work permit and residence are separate processes and no intermediary can guarantee the government's result.
items: Record the license code and type accurately
Read the employer, job and workplace restrictions
Get the list of official documents and fees from the destination government
Finalize the insurance and contract before the trip

sections.title: 4. Know your rights and responsibilities
sections.body: Once you start working, learn about minimum wage, hours, safety, insurance, taxes, and the grievance procedure. Do not jeopardize your residence status by changing your job or unemployment and notify the relevant department of any change according to the law.
items: Keep the pay slip and the contract
Save emergency and work department numbers
Do not accept informal work and the promise of salary without a contract
Record the license renewal deadline in the calendar

postDetail.sourcesNote: Working conditions depend on the country and occupation; Reference the official page of the destination government and valid contract.

post.title: Investment abroad; From assessment to legal action
post.description: A practical guide for comparing investment routes, assessing risk, reviewing documents and choosing the right destination.
post.imageAlt: A view of an international economic center

postDetail.highlight: Investment and residence are not the same concept. Check the type of capital, source of money, business risk, taxes and residency requirements separately from official sources.

sections.title: 1. Determine the goal, budget and risk tolerance
sections.body: Make it clear whether your goal is to build a business, buy shares, develop a business, or explore a residency path. Calculate the required capital, side costs and emergency reserve before choosing the country.
items: Write down the purpose of the investment
Separate the operating budget from the cost of living
Weigh the exchange rate risk and loss
Don't pay for the promise of a profit or a guaranteed stay

sections.title: 2. Compare country and program from official source
sections.body: The minimum capital, type of company, job creation, management history, legal source of money, tax and examination period are different in each country. Read the regulations from the destination's official investment, tax and immigration office.
items: Write the terms and costs in a table
Check the license and agent validity
Translate and evaluate the contract before signing
Determine the exit route from the investment

sections.title: 3. Do an independent legal and financial review
sections.body: Ownership, debt, license, bank account, tax and contract obligations should be reviewed by an independent and qualified professional. Transfer money only through legal and traceable channels.
items: Document the source of the money and receipts
Verify the identity of the seller and the company
Calculate the cost of taxes and maintenance
Consider the residence decision separately from the business decision

postDetail.sourcesNote: Investment and residence rules change; The final authority is the official offices of the destination country and licensed consultants.

post.title: Language and admission exams; The right choice and targeted preparation
post.description: A guide to choosing a test, knowing the difference between language tests and preparing an acceptable result for university, work or visa.

postDetail.highlight: Choose the right test based on the purpose and acceptance of the destination. Confirm the exam name, academic or general type, minimum score of each skill, validity date and result submission method from the university or official office.

sections.title: 1. Choose the test based on the objective
sections.body: An Academic test is usually required for university, while some work or immigration paths require a public test or a test approved by the Immigration Department. IELTS, TOEFL, PTE and destination country language tests are not automatically equivalent; Read the list of accepted tests of the same program.
items: Purpose: Specify study, work or visa
Do not confuse Academic and General
Record the minimum total score and each skill
Ask the destination organization to accept the online result

sections.title: 2. Know the format and grading
sections.body: IELTS Academic has four sections: Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking, and the test time is 2 hours and 45 minutes; But the format and time of other tests are different. Don't just practice the test by memorizing the answers: practice timing, question order, writing and speaking with an official sample.
items: Learn the time and type of questions for each section
Solve the official sample test before registering
Record your mistakes in the follow-up notebook
Do not make a memorized and unnatural answer for Speaking

sections.title: 3. Make a preparation and registration plan
sections.body: Measure the current level with a mock test and create a weekly plan based on the distance to the target score. Do not make the test date so close to the university deadline that the opportunity to repeat or send the result is lost. Read the rules of the center, ID card and allowed equipment before the test day.
items: Record the target score and submission deadline in the calendar
Practice all four skills every week
Save time to receive the result and retake the test
Match the ID card and registration details

sections.title: 4. Send the result correctly and check its validity
sections.body: The name and date of birth of the result must be the same as the passport. Send the result from the official system to the university or the relevant department and avoid sending the manipulated image. Check separately the validity of the result, the required score and the possibility of using the online test for visa.
items: Keep the result number and delivery receipt
Compare the validity date with the program start time
If the score is low, read the protest or repetition rule
For visa, choose only the exam accepted by the relevant department

postDetail.sourcesNote: The type of test and the minimum score are determined by the destination organization; Results and formats may change.
